finishStory.markedParagraph: Jacob [married] two women. He loved [Rachel] more than Leah. God let Leah have children first. She had four sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and [Judah]. Rachel could not have children, so she gave her servant [Bilhah] to Jacob as a third wife. Bilhah had two boys. Leah later gave her servant [Zilpah] to Jacob, and Zilpah also had two sons. Later, Leah had two more boys and a daughter named [Dinah]. Finally, God heard Rachel’s prayers, and she gave birth to her first son, [Joseph]. Later Rachel gave birth to another son, but she [died] soon after. Jacob named that baby [Benjamin]. Jacob’s family now included [twelve] sons and one daughter. Through this [messy] family, God still kept His [promises] and showed His faithful love.

reviewFlags.text: Original curriculum uses the ESV text of Psalm 136:1. The worksheet draft proposes the BSB translation with “loving devotion.” Verify wording and permission before approving.
Two original Important Ideas have lowercase “god” in the all-caps-styled text layer. Capitalization was corrected for display without modifying the source.
The source Story Sheet instructions refer to nine pieces, but seven labeled STORY NOTE blocks were present. Confirm whether two additional pieces exist outside the supplied ODT.
The source discusses family marriage arrangements, infertility, favoritism, and Rachel’s death. Review age-appropriate language while preserving the original theology and source facts.
Review false facts, wrong multiple-choice options, Circle the Mistakes errors, and vocabulary decoys.
Original source contains a few contextual and quoted questions; these were kept in the source-question pool and were not silently dropped.
Check whether ten name-heavy crossword clues fit the live crossword generator.
Generate and inspect all three numbered presets and confirm Preset 3 uses ten distinct True/False facts.
Teacher sign-off, official schema validation, generator testing, and booklet checks remain outstanding.
